metadata.title: Event Streaming

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for governing high‑fan‑out, publish–subscribe event distribution while constraining trust amplification and systemic risk.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Event brokers, publish–subscribe platforms, stream processors, and event distribution infrastructure.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Supporting pattern defining controlled event distribution as a high‑assurance integration surface with explicit non‑equivalence guarantees.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines events as propagation data whose distribution may amplify trust effects across systems and time.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Controls governing access control, auditability, and system interconnection in high‑fan‑out architectures (AC, AU, PL families).

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Zero Trust guidance asserting that broad distribution of authenticated data requires stricter trust mediation.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Guidance for monitoring and auditing of distributed event consumption and propagation.

metadata.remarks: Event Streaming governs publish–subscribe integrations that distribute events to multiple consumers. This pattern explicitly addresses trust amplification risk and does not imply that event production authorizes downstream actions, replay, or data persistence.

components.title: Event Producer Authorization
components.description: Controls which systems are permitted to publish events into a stream.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Unauthorized systems publishing events to induce downstream effects.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Explicit producer authorization constrains event injection.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Only authorized producers may publish events into streams.

components.title: Event Consumer Authorization
components.description: Controls which systems may subscribe to or consume events.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Unauthorized data collection through event subscription.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Explicit subscription authorization constrains event exposure.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Consumer access to event streams is restricted to least privilege.

components.title: Fan‑Out Control
components.description: Management of event distribution breadth to limit amplification and blast radius.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Abuse of broadcast mechanisms to induce widespread downstream impact.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Event distribution scope is governed and reviewable.

components.title: Event Non-Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Explicitly defines what receipt or emission of events does not grant or imply.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Non‑equivalence guarantees prevent over‑trust of event effects.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Events do not imply authorization, correctness, or entitlement for downstream actions.
